name: list_windows
description: List windows and their process and window IDs. Filter by app name, bundle ID, or pid.

app.description: Only windows of apps with a name that contains this text (case-insensitive), or whose bundle id equals it. On macOS an app answers to its shown, possibly localized name and to its bundle's own name, so `Calculator` matches on every system language. Prefer this or `pid` over an unfiltered call, which returns every window on the host.

on_screen_only.description: Drop windows not on the current Space.

pid.description: Only this pid's windows, on every layer.

session.description: For multi-call work, prefer a short public session label and repeat it on every call that accepts it.

name: get_window_state
description: Read a window's accessibility tree and screenshot. In the default Markdown tree, address row N as element_token <snapshot_id>:N. Use tree_format elements for structured tokens. Reading the same window again replaces its previous snapshot. Use since to read changes after an action.

capture_mode.description: DEPRECATED and ignored. get_window_state always returns BOTH the element tree and a screenshot — ground on both. The modality is chosen at action time by how you address the target: an element ax action (element_token) or an element px action (x,y). Any value (including the old "som"/"screenshot" aliases) is accepted but has no effect.

display_only.description: Default false. With include_accessibility_tree:false, returns pixels for display without registering an action capture or replacing the agent snapshot. The image cannot ground input actions.

full_output.description: Default false. Set true to restore the previous full response: both `elements` and `tree_markdown`, all metadata, and the platform's own walk limits unless max_elements / max_depth are passed. Does not combine with `since`.

include_accessibility_tree.description: Default true. False skips the AX walk and returns the screenshot plus window metadata. Both this and include_screenshot false is an error.

include_screenshot.description: Default true. False returns the tree only (saves image tokens and latency); screenshot_out_file still forces a capture.

max_dimension.description: Optional cap on the returned screenshot's long edge, in pixels (aspect ratio preserved) — the cheap path for a small preview / thumbnail. Applied on top of the session/global max_image_dimension ceiling; the tighter of the two wins. Omit for the configured default.

max_elements.description: Cap on AX nodes walked (depth-first; markdown and elements truncate together). Default 250 (2 000 with full_output:true); the response states when the tree was cut.

max_image_dimension.description: Per-call override for the returned screenshot's long edge in pixels. An explicit value wins over the session/global setting; 0 returns native resolution. Omit to preserve configured behavior.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter; `a|b` matches rows containing either. Returns matching rows plus ancestors, or says `0 of N elements match` when none does; element_index values are not renumbered. Try this before a full read.

screenshot_format.description: Encoding of the returned screenshot. Default "png". "jpeg" is smaller, drops alpha, and mints no capture_id (capture_id-bound tools need a PNG read); pixel coordinates are unchanged.

screenshot_out_file.description: When set, write the screenshot (PNG, or JPEG with screenshot_format:"jpeg") to this file path (~ expanded) instead of embedding base64 in the response. The structured output will contain screenshot_file_path instead.

screenshot_quality.description: JPEG quality, 1-95, with screenshot_format:"jpeg" only. Default 85.

session.description: For multi-call work, prefer a short public session label and repeat it on every call that accepts it.

since.description: A `snapshot_id` from an earlier get_window_state of the same window, or "latest" for this window's most recent read with the same query/max_elements/max_depth. Use it on every re-read after acting. Returns only what changed against that snapshot: `+` added rows, `~` changed rows, `-` removed rows (removed ids are the old snapshot's), or `no change`. Falls back to a full read when the snapshot is unknown, expired, belongs to another window, or was read with a different query/max_elements/max_depth; `since_status` says which. The response still carries a NEW snapshot_id and its element_tokens; rows not listed keep their previous [N] unless a `reindexed:` line says otherwise. Every tree read also returns the window's `ui_tree_revision`: it stays the same while reads of the same view see the same rows, and grows when they change. Pass it as `ui_tree_revision` on an action to have the action refused with `stale_revision`, before any input, when a later read saw the tree change.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock budget in milliseconds for the accessibility-tree walk (default 1000, min 100, max 120000). Bounds the WHOLE walk. When the budget runs out the tool returns the PARTIAL tree it has, flagged with `truncated: true`, `truncation_reason`, `nodes_visited`, `nodes_pending` and `elements_complete: false`; retry with a larger value (e.g. 5000) or narrow with `query` / `max_depth`.

tree_format.description: Which tree representation to return. Default "markdown": the compact `tree_markdown` only, where a row `[N]` is addressed with element_token `<snapshot_id>:N`. "elements": the structured `elements` array only (per-element element_token, frame, parent_index, value), plus `observations`: display-only rows such as static text, with role, label, value and frame but no element_token, for reading and verify_state only. "both": the two together, as before; roughly doubles the size.

verbose.description: Default false. Set true to include the `_note` string and the full `background_input` capability report (macOS), which are omitted by default to save context.

name: click
description: Click a window element by element_token from the latest snapshot, or by x and y in that window's screenshot.

action.description: AX action: press (default), show_menu, pick, confirm, cancel, open, show_alternate_ui, show_default_ui; or an element's published custom_actions name or raw envelope. show_alternate_ui reveals hover-only controls on an element that lists it, without the pointer.

capture_id.description: Optional capture ID from get_window_state or get_desktop_state. With x,y it is consumed atomically; stale or mismatched captures are refused.

debug_image_out.description: Write a screenshot with a crosshair at (x, y) to this path. Needs window_id; not with from_zoom.

delivery_mode.description: Default "background" (no fronting). "foreground" briefly fronts the window, acts, then restores the prior app; needs window_id and is required for modified clicks. Escalate in order: AX element_token, background pixel, foreground, checking state between rungs; a click has no read-back except list-row selection.

element_token.description: Element handle `<snapshot_id>:<row>` from get_window_state: row `[11]` of snapshot s0000002a is "s0000002a:11".

from_zoom.description: x and y are in the last zoom image for this pid.

modifier.description: Modifier keys: cmd, shift, option/alt, ctrl.

pid.description: Target process ID. Optional with element_token (it carries the pid).

post_action_wait.description: "none" returns without waiting up to 300 ms for a new window, menu, dialog or foreground change; a change seen later is reported on the next action's result.

scope.description: Default "window". "desktop": x,y with no pid/window_id are true screen pixels from get_desktop_state.

session.description: For multi-call work, prefer a short public session label and repeat it on every call that accepts it.

target.description: Exact window (kind "window", with pid and window_id) or desktop (kind "desktop", with display_id). "primary" is the portable desktop target.

ui_tree_revision.description: The `ui_tree_revision` of the get_window_state read this action was planned from. The action is refused with `stale_revision`, before any input is delivered, when a later read of the same window saw the tree change or the driver has no revision for the window. It covers changes a read has observed: the driver does not watch the window between reads.

window_id.description: Target window ID. Omit with element_token.

x.description: X in screenshot pixels (get_window_state PNG, or get_desktop_state PNG for a desktop target).

y.description: Y in screenshot pixels from the image selected by target.

name: type_text
description: Insert text into the element named by element_token or into the focused field of the target window.

delay_ms.description: Ms between characters in the CGEvent fallback. Default 0: characters go in batched key events, fast. Set a positive value for one paced key per character (debounced search boxes).

delivery_mode.description: Default "background": AX insert, then CGEvent keys, no focus steal. "foreground": front the window, type, restore; last resort for surfaces (WhatsApp/Catalyst) where background keys do not land.

element_token.description: Element handle `<snapshot_id>:<row>` from get_window_state: row `[11]` of snapshot s0000002a is "s0000002a:11".

post_action_wait.description: "none" returns without waiting up to 300 ms for a new window, menu, dialog or foreground change; a change seen later is reported on the next action's result.

scope.description: "desktop" with no pid/window_id types into the frontmost app.

session.description: For multi-call work, prefer a short public session label and repeat it on every call that accepts it.

target.description:
Preferred per-call target: an exact window (`kind="window"`, `pid`, `window_id`) or the
primary desktop (`kind="desktop"`, `display_id="primary"`).

ui_tree_revision.description: The `ui_tree_revision` of the get_window_state read this action was planned from. The action is refused with `stale_revision`, before any input is delivered, when a later read of the same window saw the tree change or the driver has no revision for the window. It covers changes a read has observed: the driver does not watch the window between reads.

x.description: Screenshot-pixel X of the field (get_window_state PNG, as in click). With y and no element_token, pixel-clicks to focus, then types.

name: press_key
description: Press and release a key in the target window or element. Key names include return, tab, escape, arrows, space, delete, home, end, pageup, pagedown, function keys, letters, and digits.

delivery_mode.description: Default "background": no fronting or focus steal. "foreground": briefly front the window, act, restore the prior app; last resort when background did not land.

element_token.description: Element handle `<snapshot_id>:<row>` from get_window_state: row `[11]` of snapshot s0000002a is "s0000002a:11".

post_action_wait.description: "none" returns without waiting up to 300 ms for a new window, menu, dialog or foreground change; a change seen later is reported on the next action's result.

scope.description: "desktop" with no pid/window_id sends to the frontmost app.

session.description: For multi-call work, prefer a short public session label and repeat it on every call that accepts it.

target.description:
Preferred per-call target: an exact window (`kind="window"`, `pid`, `window_id`) or the
primary desktop (`kind="desktop"`, `display_id="primary"`).

ui_tree_revision.description: The `ui_tree_revision` of the get_window_state read this action was planned from. The action is refused with `stale_revision`, before any input is delivered, when a later read of the same window saw the tree change or the driver has no revision for the window. It covers changes a read has observed: the driver does not watch the window between reads.

window_id.description: Target window; required for foreground. Does not raise by itself.

x.description: Screenshot-pixel X: pixel-click to focus, then send the key. With y, no element_token.
